title: Micro-annotation & Stack-context playbook for compact trace rows
content:
Context / goal:
This note collects rapid design experiments for a compact trace row that surfaces service-level context and lets engineers add tiny, structured annotations without leaving the trace view. The aim: make dense trace lists scannable at a glance and actionable (jump to logs, create a quick bug note, pin span) while keeping waterfall legible.

Why this feels important now:
- We keep hearing that long traces + wide water-falls are impossible to scan on smaller monitors; teams prefer dense lists for triage.
- Current inspector modal is heavyweight — people want to jot a quick note or file a follow-up from the trace list itself.
- We want to reduce time-to-first-action when investigating high-latency traces.

Key concepts (short):
- Compact span row: 1.5x height, minimal chrome, shows service, op name, duration, error marker, 1-line summary and a micro-context pill.
- Stack-context pill: displays upstream service affinity (2 small avatars / service initials), last deploy timestamp (relative), and an error-score microbar. Hover reveals short tooltips.
- Micro-annotation composer: inline, minimal composer attached to a span row (text <=140 chars + tags + quick actions).
- Quick-action shelf: small icon set on the right of the row that appears on hover or keyboard focus (logs, goto-trace, create-issue, pin).

Wireframe / interactions (sketch-level):
1) Default compact row layout (left to right):
   - left: span time offset marker (thin vertical tick aligned to waterfall),
   - next: service short name (bold, 10px), op name (mono, truncated), duration (right-aligned),
   - center: condensed waterfall mini-bar showing the span relative width, with tiny token-level gradient if available (placeholder color spectrum),
   - right: stack-context pill + quick-action icons hidden until hover.

2) Hover interaction:
   - hovering the row expands it by 6px and fades in quick-action shelf.
   - hover on stack-context pill opens a 200px wide popup with 3 rows: "Top upstream: service-a (45%), last deploy 2h ago", "Recent errors: 3/100", "Hot traces: 12 in last 5m".
   - the tiny waterfall mini-bar supports scrub (mouse move) to display token counts / KV cache hits as a small tooltip.

3) Micro-annotation composer flow:
   - trigger: click the small pencil icon or press keyboard shortcut 'a' when row focused.
   - composer opens inline replacing the 1-line summary with a lightweight input: placeholder "Add quick note (link logs with #)".
   - composer supports tags via @ (service) and # (ticket). Press Enter to save.
   - saved annotation appears as a tiny capsule under the op name (author initials + 1line), tappable to expand full note in side rail.

4) Pin & share:
   - Pin puts span into a "shortlist" tray at top of trace view (persisted in session).
   - From shortlist, users can multi-select spans and open a share dialog to generate a short URL or create a Jira with prefilled context.

Accessibility / keyboard-first behavior:
- Tab / Shift-Tab navigates rows; arrow keys scrub time; 'a' opens composer; 'p' pins; 'g' goes to logs; '/' focuses filter.
- Ensure contrast for compact text; allow users to switch to relaxed row spacing in settings.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Compact row layout implemented for list view + waterfall mini-bar, responsive to widths >= 900px.
- Hover quick-action shelf with at least 3 actions (logs, pin, create-issue) wired to existing routes.
- Inline composer that saves annotations to trace metadata (visible under same trace on reload).
- Stack-context pill that pulls upstream service stat + last deploy timestamp from product API.
- Keyboard shortcuts documented in console shortcuts panel.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Data model: where do quick-annotations live? Prefer trace-level metadata (visible to teammates) vs ephemeral local notes. MVP: persist in trace metadata with author attribution.
- Privacy & RBAC: should all teams be able to write annotations? We need a quick permissions check. Tie to project-level write perms.
- Performance: inline composer should not trigger heavy network calls; debounce and optimistic UI.
- Mobile: compact rows probably not ideal on very small screens. Consider a separate "mobile view" with collapsed span selection.

Backlog/tasks (rough priorities):
- TRC-924: compact row baseline + CSS tokens (1 week) [owner: frontend]
- TRC-931: mini-waterfall canvas + scrub tooltip (2 sprints) [owner: rendering eng]
- TRC-942: micro-annotation API & persistence (backend + migrations) (2 sprints) [owner: api team]
- TRC-956: quick-action integrations (logs, create-jira) (1 sprint) [owner: integrations]
- TRC-980: keyboard shortcuts & accessibility pass (1 sprint) [owner: sxe]

Prototyping notes / experiments to try: 
- Try an inline compositor that auto-suggests relevant logs when user types a '#' — do a small eval with 8 internal engineers.
- A/B test: compact rows vs current density on triage speed for a curated set of traces. Measure "time to first action".
- Micro-annotation visibility: experiment with public vs private toggle for an annotation. Track engagement.

Edge cases & nitty-gritty:
- Very long op names: truncate with middle ellipsis, hover to show full.
- Synchronized hover: when you hover a row, optionally highlight corresponding spans in the waterfall by increasing opacity. This must be toggleable (perf).
- When traces are sampled or incomplete, show subtle badge "partial" in stack-context pill.

Related links & references:
- design file (see linked_artifacts), PR for compact CSS variables, previous convo in #console-ux 2025-10-28.

Next steps for this doc:
- Bring to product grooming (Mon 2026-02-20).
- Ask backend for a simple schema for annotations (fields: id, trace_id, span_id, author, text, tags, created_at, visibility).
- Quick spike: Miguel to prototype inline composer in storybook by 2026-02-26.

Notes to reviewers (what I want feedback on):
- Is inline composer useful or noisy? (voice of SREs vs devs)
- Which quick-actions are most used — should we include 're-run request' as an action?
- Privacy model: public by default or private by default?

Rough sketches (verbal):
- Sketch A: dense 1.5x rows, stack-pill right, minimal icons, waterfall center.
- Sketch B: slightly larger rows with avatars for top upstream, colored error dot after service name, composer inline pushes other rows down.
- Sketch C: keyboard-first with focus ring, ephemeral popover for composer instead of inlining.

-- end --

Unresolved: priority between immersive inspector vs inline micro-actions — need product call.
